findings.text: D8 forbids every proof about a migrated kind from unfolding `runScriptStep`, including the kind rule’s own proof, which D1 and D12 explicitly permit. Fix: Apply this restriction to callers of the kind rule and exempt the proof that establishes it.

`runScriptStep_insertSelect_ok` accepts an arbitrary `returning` list, so the slice 6 rule for an empty list cannot replace its proof for statements with RETURNING. Fix: Keep `runScriptStep_copyOf` as the slice 6 example and classify `runScriptStep_insertSelect_ok` as a group law under D5.
D8 says retention tests are temporary while owner decision 3 is open and option (b) keeps them indefinitely. Fix: Make the lifetime conditional on owner decision 3.

D12 requires callers for more than one kind even when option (b) leaves part of a group without a rule, whereas D5 requires the group law to stay until its last kind has a rule. Fix: Apply the caller-count condition only after every kind in the group has a rule.

D12 permits a theorem such as the pilot’s `runScriptStep_insert_ok` to pass the final check because it proves a complete step from the kind rule, although D7 explicitly forbids this one-case law. Fix: Include D7’s prohibition on one theorem per case in the final check.

The text check can pass after `Sql.check_send_of_step` is deleted even though the `sql_run` diagnostic in `SqlRunGoals.lean` still tells users to apply it and `S6AutoShapes.lean` checks that message. Fix: Include user-facing diagnostics and their expected messages in the same-slice text update.

The blanket ban on naming deleted laws conflicts with the retained witnesses under owner option 3(b), whose docstrings identify the deleted formulas they check. Fix: Exempt docstrings that identify a deleted law as the subject of a retained witness.
